headline: 75,000 depositors seek to withdraw nearly Tk 4,000cr from Sammilito Islami Bank
summary: Around 75,000 customers have applied to withdraw nearly Tk 4,000 crore from Sammilito Islami Bank, formed by merging five troubled Islamic banks. The Bangladesh Bank has provided Tk 5,000 crore liquidity to facilitate these payments and restore depositor confi
details: In the first four days of this month, approximately 75,000 customers have applied to withdraw their deposits from Sammilito Islami Bank. The total amount sought by these applicants is Tk 3,925 crore, according to bank officials.

Sammilito Islami Bank, established last year through the merger of five struggling Islamic banks (First Security Islami Bank, Global Islami Bank, Social Islami Bank, Union Bank, and EXIM Bank), began disbursing the requested funds today.

The Bangladesh Bank (BB) on Sunday provided Tk 5,000 crore in liquidity support to the newly formed bank. This intervention aims to enable the bank to meet customer withdrawal demands and resume normal banking operations.

The central bank's payment initiative is designed to restore confidence among depositors of the merged banks, which had previously faced severe liquidity and governance issues. The central bank has also announced a scheme to repay the entire amount to depositors in phases.

On August 25, the BB confirmed there would be no "haircut" on deposits for Sammilito Islami Bank customers. It also announced that individual depositors could withdraw the principal amount of their deposits as needed starting from September 1.

Following this announcement, Sammilito Islami Bank accepted applications from customers until Sunday. Bank officials stated that applications were processed according to prescribed rules, requiring customers to visit their respective branches or sub-branches for submission.
Officials confirmed they would verify all applications before handing over the money to depositors. This process ensures that all due amounts are paid accurately and efficiently.

The central bank's payment initiative is designed to restore confidence among depositors of the merged banks, which had previously faced severe liquidity and governance issues. The central bank has also announced a scheme to repay the entire amount to depositors in phases.

On August 25, the BB confirmed there would be no "haircut" on deposits for Sammilito Islami Bank customers. It also announced that individual depositors could withdraw the principal amount of their deposits as needed starting from September 1.

headline: Bangladesh's foreign exchange reserves rise to $36 billion, enough for four months of imports
summary: Bangladesh's foreign exchange reserves have significantly increased over the past two years, now sufficient to cover four months of import expenses. This surpasses the internationally accepted standard of three months.
details: Bangladesh's foreign exchange reserves have significantly increased over the past two years. The Bangladesh Bank now holds enough reserves to cover four months of import expenses.
This amount, standing at $36.39 billion (3,639 crore) as of Sunday, is well above the internationally accepted standard of three months' import coverage.
The reserves have grown by approximately $3 billion in the last six months alone. This indicates a positive trend in the country's economic stability.
Bangladesh Bank also reported that the reserves had exceeded $37.5 billion just last week, showcasing dynamic fluctuations in the foreign currency market.
